what: FedEx Freight is the largest less-than-truckload carrier in North America, spun out of FedEx as a separate company. It moves pallet-sized shipments from many customers on shared trailers through its own terminal network.
customers: Manufacturers, retailers and distributors shipping freight too large for parcel and too small for a full truck.
money: shipments moved through its terminal network
moat: A national terminal network and the service record that comes with it, in an industry where adding capacity means buying scarce industrial land near cities.
risks: Freight volumes have been weak across the industry for three years
Debt of about $6.3 billion taken on at the spin-off
It is newly independent with a short record as a standalone company
opportunities: Analysts see about 13% upside from current levels
Operating independently allows pricing and network decisions that suited the parent less well
A freight recovery would flow through to profits quickly given spare capacity
watch: Tonnage per day, revenue per hundredweight, and the operating ratio.
